**04/29/2024 2:20 PM –** Reyes returned my call. He said the report was drafted but he was waiting on one photograph from his assistant to finalize it. He expected to send it by 05/01/2024. I thanked him and noted the expected date in the file. LN.

**04/30/2024 10:30 AM –** Client called. She said she had received a text from the landlord’s property manager asking whether she planned to renew the lease. She replied that she was still deciding. She asked if this was a problem. I told her it was fine, and that the extension was in writing, so the landlord could not pressure her. I also reminded her that the inspection report should be ready soon. RO.

**05/01/2024 11:00 AM –** Received the inspection report from Reyes via email. The report is dated 05/01/2024 and includes 14 pages of findings and photographs. Key findings: (1) visible condensation on the underside of the roof deck near the vent pipe in the hallway attic access, consistent with the onsite observation; (2) evidence of past water intrusion in the ceiling of the bedroom closet, with staining that appears to have been painted over; (3) the patched areas in the living room and bedroom are cosmetic and do not address the source of moisture; (4) the bathroom exhaust fan vents into the attic rather than to the exterior, which Reyes states is a contributing factor; (5) no active mold growth was observed at the time of inspection, but conditions are conducive. Reyes recommends a licensed contractor evaluate the roof and venting, and suggests a moisture meter test of the affected areas. I forwarded the report to M.C. and to the client. LN.

**05/01/2024 2:00 PM –** M.C. reviewed the report and asked me to draft a summary for her review. She also said we should send the landlord a formal letter putting them on notice of the defects and requesting repair. She asked me to include the report as an attachment. I began drafting the letter. RO.

documents.content:
03/13/2024 2:20 PM – Client called. Reports she found a small patch of black-colored growth on the ceiling of the bathroom, near the exhaust fan, that was not there in her 03/09 photos. She took a new photo (IMG_4471) and emailed it to us. Noted in photo log. Advised client not to clean or disturb the area until we can arrange an inspection. RO.

03/14/2024 10:00 AM – Contacted Harborview Code Enforcement. Spoke with Inspector M. Chen. He has prior history on this property from a 2022 complaint (closed). He agreed to schedule an inspection of unit 4B based on our letter and client photos. Anticipated date 03/18/2024. Will confirm via email. RO.

03/14/2024 3:45 PM – Received return receipt for verification request (signed by "T. Bell" on 03/13/2024). Filed in correspondence tab. LN.

03/18/2024 9:30 AM – Inspection conducted by Code Enforcement Inspector M. Chen at unit 4B. Client was present. I (RO) was not on site; client reported inspector spent approx. 45 min, took photos, and used a moisture meter in the bathroom and closet. Inspector did not speak with landlord representative; no one from Wescott Properties attended. Client will email us a copy of any inspection report she receives. Pending written report. RO.

03/18/2024 2:10 PM – Client forwarded Code Enforcement inspection report (received by her via email from Inspector Chen, dated 03/18/2024). Report references Inspection Form A-12 signed by inspector. Key findings: moisture intrusion from leaking vent pipe in bathroom ceiling; elevated moisture readings in bathroom wall and bedroom closet wall; visible fungal growth consistent with mold in bathroom ceiling and closet wall; recommendation for remediation by licensed contractor and repair of vent pipe. Report lists unit 4B has_mold: confirmed (inspection form). Status: current finding as of inspection date. Full report scanned to evidence folder. RO.

03/19/2024 11:15 AM – Called Wescott Properties (T. Bell) to discuss inspection findings and demand remediation. Left voicemail. Also sent follow-up email with copy of the inspection report attached, requesting response by 03/25/2024. No response as of COB. RO.

Unit 4B has_mold: confirmed (inspection form). Record status: current.

03/20/2024 9:50 AM – Client called. She is concerned about health symptoms (cough, sinus congestion) she attributes to the mold. She is also worried about her lease renewal, which is up in June. We discussed options: repair-and-deduct, potential breach of warranty of habitability, and possible relocation if conditions worsen. Client wants to proceed with repair-and-deduct. She will obtain two contractor estimates for remediation. RO.

03/21/2024 1:30 PM – Received email from T. Bell (Wescott Properties). He disputes the inspection findings, claims the report is "preliminary" and that the inspector did not take air samples. He states they will "look into it" but provides no timeline. I replied requesting a written response by 03/25/2024 and reminded him of the verification request deadline (03/26/2024). No further response yet. RO.

03/22/2024 10:05 AM – Client dropped off two contractor estimates: (1) All-Clear Environmental, $2,450 for mold remediation of bathroom and closet, plus vent pipe repair; (2) Harborview Restoration, $3,100 for remediation, pipe repair, and repainting. Estimates filed in evidence folder. Client states costs are consistent with amounts she found online. LN.

03/25/2024 4:00 PM – No response from Wescott Properties to our 03/19 email or 03/21 reply. Verification request response also not received by deadline (due 03/26/2024). RO to follow up tomorrow.

03/26/2024 9:15 AM – Called Wescott Properties. Spoke with T. Bell directly. He again disputed the inspection, said they are "reviewing" options, and would not commit to a date for remediation. He did not provide the requested maintenance records. I advised him that we intend to proceed with repair-and-deduct if no remediation plan is provided by 04/02/2024. He said he would "get back to us." RO.

documents.title: Case Management Records

04/04/2024 9:00 AM – Sent letter to Wescott Properties via email and certified mail requesting reimbursement for the two inspection reports (dated 03/18 and 03/25, total $650) and the contractor estimates ($75 for All-Clear, $60 for Harborview). Not strictly required for repair-and-deduct but included to preserve the claim for damages. LN to draft and send.

04/08/2024 10:30 AM – Received voicemail from T. Bell (Wescott). He says they have "retained counsel" and that all further communication should go through their attorney. No attorney name or contact info left in the voicemail. I called back and left a message requesting the attorney's details in writing. RO.

04/09/2024 3:45 PM – Client called re: mold. She says the smell is worse in the bathroom and she found new discoloration on the closet ceiling. She took photos and will email them. I advised her to document the date/time and to keep the photos in a folder. She is still holding off on scheduling remediation per our earlier discussion. RO.

04/10/2024 11:00 AM – Received email from A. Patel, Esq. (Patel & Singh LLP) representing Wescott Properties. He states that his client disputes the findings and will not authorize any remediation until an independent inspection is conducted. He proposes a joint inspection with an agreed-upon third-party inspector. He also states that the lease does not require the landlord to address conditions that are "caused by tenant use or neglect," and suggests the mold may be from the tenant's failure to ventilate the bathroom. I replied requesting (1) the name of the proposed inspector, (2) a date for the inspection, and (3) confirmation that the landlord will cover the cost of the independent inspection. I also noted that our client disputes the characterization of the mold as tenant-caused and that the vent pipe issue appears to be a maintenance matter. RO.

04/11/2024 1:00 PM – Client called after receiving a copy of the lease renewal notice (due 06/30/2024). She is worried that the landlord will not renew if she pursues repair-and-deduct. I explained that the renewal is a separate issue and that retaliation is prohibited, but we should document any non-renewal if it occurs. She wants to know if she should sign the renewal. I advised her to wait until the mold issue is resolved, but to be aware of the deadline. She will bring the renewal notice to our next meeting. LN.

04/12/2024 9:30 AM – Case File CF-2024-034 case_status: active (case management system). Record status: current. No change. RO.

04/15/2024 2:00 PM – Received email from A. Patel. He proposes a joint inspection on 04/22/2024 at 10:00 AM with "Building Insights Inspections" as the third-party firm. He states the landlord will cover the inspection cost. He also requests that our client be present for the inspection. I confirmed the date/time with the client and replied to Patel accepting the proposal, with the condition that the inspector also examine the vent pipe and any related plumbing. Client confirmed availability. RO.

04/16/2024 10:15 AM – Client dropped off a copy of the lease renewal notice. Reviewed it. The renewal is for a one-year term at the same rent, with no changes to the lease terms. I noted that the lease has a clause about "tenant responsibility for cleanliness" which Patel may rely on. I will research whether this clause has been interpreted to cover mold in similar cases. LN.

04/17/2024 3:00 PM – Spoke with client by phone. She is concerned that the independent inspector will side with the landlord. I explained that the purpose of the joint inspection is to get an objective assessment, and that we will have the opportunity to question the inspector's findings. She agreed to be present and will bring her photos. I also reminded her to keep a log of any new symptoms or changes in the mold condition. RO.

**Case File CF-2024-034 – Chronological Log (continued)**

**04/19/2024 9:05 AM –** Client called. She said the mold in the bathroom has spread to the ceiling above the shower. She sent two photos by text. The photos show dark spots along the ceiling seam and what looks like peeling paint near the vent pipe. I told her not to clean the area until the inspector sees it, and to keep the photos with timestamps. She confirmed she will attend the inspection on 04/22. RO.

**04/19/2024 1:45 PM –** Left voicemail for A. Patel confirming that our client will be present at the joint inspection on 04/22 at 10:00 AM. Asked that the inspector bring a moisture meter and check the vent pipe connection. No return call yet. LN.

**04/20/2024 10:30 AM –** Reviewed lease clause on "tenant responsibility for cleanliness." The clause is broad and could be read to include mold prevention, but I found two appellate cases in this state where similar clauses were held not to shift liability for latent defects. I printed both cases and placed them in the file. Will discuss with supervising attorney on Monday. LN.

**04/20/2024 2:15 PM –** Client emailed the two photos from yesterday and also a photo of the lease renewal notice with the deadline highlighted. She asked again whether she should sign. I replied that we will have a clearer answer after the inspection, and that she should not sign before we talk. RO.

**04/21/2024 11:00 AM –** No office hours. Client called and left a message: she is worried the landlord will evict her if she does not sign the renewal. She said she has never been late on rent. I will call her back Monday morning before the inspection. LN.

**04/22/2024 9:50 AM –** Met client in the lobby. She brought her photo log and the renewal notice. We walked to the unit together. A. Patel and the inspector from Building Insights Inspections were already there. The inspector introduced himself as D. Reyes, license #IN-88421. He had a moisture meter and a borescope.

**04/22/2024 10:00 AM – 11:40 AM –** Joint inspection conducted. Inspector Reyes examined the bathroom, the vent pipe, the ceiling above the shower, and the exterior wall near the kitchen. He took photos and noted readings. Patel was present for the entire inspection. Client pointed out the areas that had been patched by the landlord in March. Reyes said the patches were cosmetic and did not address the source. He also checked the attic access in the hallway and found what he described as "visible condensation on the underside of the roof deck" near the vent pipe. He did not give a verbal conclusion, but he said he would prepare a written report within 5–7 business days. I took my own notes and photos. RO.

**04/22/2024 1:30 PM –** Debrief with client at the office. She said she felt the inspector was thorough and neutral. I told her we will wait for the written report before deciding next steps. She asked if she should sign the renewal now. I advised her to hold off until we receive the report and discuss with the attorney. She agreed. LN.

**04/23/2024 9:15 AM –** Received call from A. Patel. He said the landlord is willing to extend the deadline for the lease renewal by 14 days so that the inspection report can be reviewed. He asked if our client would agree to a short extension. I told him I would confirm with the client and get back to him by end of day. RO.

**04/23/2024 11:00 AM –** Called client. She agreed to the 14-day extension. I emailed Patel confirming the extension, and asked that the landlord provide the extension in writing. Patel replied that he would send a short addendum by email. LN.

**04/23/2024 3:20 PM –** Received the addendum from Patel. It states the renewal deadline is extended to 05/06/2024. The addendum is signed by Patel and the landlord. I forwarded it to the client and asked her to sign a copy for our records. RO.

**04/24/2024 10:00 AM –** Supervising attorney review. I presented the two appellate cases to M.C. She agreed they are on point and said we can rely on them if the landlord argues the cleanliness clause. She also noted that the inspection report will be the key document. M.C. asked me to prepare a summary of the inspection findings once the report is received. LN.
